description: Send one key action through the formed desktop session and return backend evidence. Requires current gui.control ownership and a fresh single-use gui.observe observation. Posted input is not proof of the application outcome; observe again.

key.description: Lowercase physical macOS key names, ANSI positions independent of current keyboard layout; use gui.type for Unicode text. Optional unique cmd+, ctrl+, alt+, shift+, fn+ modifiers. Examples: cmd+shift+p, ctrl+alt+delete, f12, keypadenter. Supported keys: a, s, d, f, h, g, z, x, c, v, b, q, w, e, r, y, t, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 5, equal, 9, 7, minus, 8, 0, rightbracket, o, u, leftbracket, i, p, l, j, quote, k, semicolon, backslash, comma, slash, n, m, period, grave, keypaddecimal, keypadmultiply, keypadplus, keypadclear, keypaddivide, keypadenter, keypadminus, keypadequals, keypad0, keypad1, keypad2, keypad3, keypad4, keypad5, keypad6, keypad7, keypad8, keypad9, enter, tab, space, backspace, escape, cmd, shift, capslock, alt, ctrl, rightcmd, rightshift, rightalt, rightctrl, fn, f17, volumeup, volumedown, mute, f18, f19, f20, f5, f6, f7, f3, f8, f9, f11, f13, f16, f14, f10, contextualmenu, f12, f15, help, home, pageup, delete, f4, end, f2, pagedown, f1, left, right, down, up, isosection, jisyen, jisunderscore, jiskeypadcomma, jiseisu, jiskana

screen_id.description: Exact screen id from gui.status; coordinates use this screenshot pixel domain.
